summary: DialectSpec dataclass and DIALECTS registry — the data-driven heart of the Ibis backend. DialectSpec holds ibis_backend_name, connection_mode, connection_string_scheme, connection_builder, and optional capability hooks (upsert, create_index, drop_index, rename_table, index SQL generators). DIALECTS maps 20 dialect names to DialectSpec entries. Connection builders for all dialects are in this file.
extension_points: DIALECTS dict — add a new entry with a DialectSpec to register a new ibis dialect
DialectSpec.connection_builder — the factory callable (**config) -> ibis backend
Optional hooks: upsert_hook, create_index_hook, drop_index_hook, rename_table_hook, get_index_exists_sql, get_list_indexes_sql
lifecycle_notes: 20 dialects: sqlite, duckdb, motherduck, postgres, mysql, mssql, oracle, snowflake, bigquery, redshift, trino, clickhouse, databricks, singlestoredb, exasol, impala, materialize, risingwave, druid, pyspark.
redshift reuses _build_postgres_connection — it rides on the postgres ibis protocol.
motherduck ibis_backend_name is 'duckdb' — shares duckdb's ibis backend but different URL pattern.
Connection mode constants: CONNECTION_STRING, KWARGS, HYBRID — mirror IBIS_DB_CONNECTION_MODE enum.
documentation_hooks: DIALECTS is the source of truth for 'which databases are supported' — reference docs should generate from it
Capability hooks table: which dialects support upsert, create_index, etc. — important for users choosing a backend
risks: Connection builders import ibis at call time (lazy) — ImportError surface differs from module load time
